ai.literal: Not departing if there is, to me tell; otherwise, your quick return, to those who survive, tell.
ai.translation: If you are not departing, tell me; but as for your quick return, tell that to those who will survive until then.
ai.modern: நீ போகாமல் இருக்கப் போகிறாய் என்றால் அதை என்னிடம் சொல்; மாறாக, நீ சீக்கிரம் திரும்பி வருவதைப் பற்றி, நீ இல்லாத காலத்தில் உயிர் பிழைத்திருப்பவர்களிடம் சொல்.
ai.explanation: The heroine speaks to her departing lover, unable to bear the grief of separation. She tells him that if he has decided not to leave, he should tell her that happy news. However, if he is indeed leaving and promises a quick return, he should tell that to those who can survive the grief of separation; she herself will not survive to hear of his return.

ai.literal: Pleasure possesses his gaze; separation-fearing sorrow possesses indeed union.
ai.translation: The gaze of my beloved brings pure pleasure; but our very union is filled with the sorrow of fearing a future separation.
ai.modern: அவருடைய பார்வை இன்பம் தருவதாக இருக்கிறது; ஆனால் எங்களது சேர்க்கையோ, பிரிவை நினைத்து அஞ்சுகின்ற துன்பத்தைக் கொண்டதாக இருக்கிறது.
ai.explanation: This couplet portrays the bittersweet anxiety of a lover. The heroine explains that merely looking at her beloved ('பார்வல்') brings her pure joy ('இன்கண்'). However, the actual physical union ('புணர்வு') is shadowed by 'புன்கண்' (sorrow), because the moment they are together, she is gripped by the fear of their next inevitable separation ('பிரிவஞ்சும்'). The contrast between the simple joy of his gaze and the complex anxiety of their embrace highlights the intensity of her attachment.

ai.literal: Difficult indeed is consolation, even in those who possess wisdom, because separation exists at a certain time.
ai.translation: Consolation is indeed difficult to find, even in those who possess great wisdom, because separation is a reality that inevitably occurs at some time.
ai.modern: அறிவுடையவர்களிடத்திலும் தேறுதல் அடைவது மிகவும் அரிதானது; ஏனெனில், ஏதோ ஒரு காலத்தில் பிரிவு என்பது உண்மையாகவே நிகழ்ந்துவிடுகிறது.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the overwhelming pain of parting, which can shatter even the most disciplined minds. The speaker notes that finding consolation or clarity of mind (தேற்றம்) is extremely difficult (அரிது), even among highly wise and mature individuals (அறிவுடையார் கண்ணும்). This is because separation (பிரிவு) is an inevitable reality that occurs at some point (ஓர் இடத்து உண்மையான்). The verse beautifully shows that the emotional suffering of parting transcends intellectual wisdom and self-control.

ai.literal: Having shown love, he who said 'do not fear', if he departs, the assured word, to those who believed, is there a fault?
ai.translation: If he who lovingly comforted me saying 'do not fear' now departs, is it the fault of those who believed his reassuring words?
ai.modern: அன்பு காட்டி, 'அஞ்சாதே' என்று சொன்னவர் நம்மை விட்டுப் பிரிந்தால், அவருடைய தெளிவான வார்த்தைகளை நம்பியவர்களிடம் ஏதேனும் தவறு இருக்க முடியுமா?
ai.explanation: This couplet expresses the grief and sense of betrayal felt by the heroine when her lover departs. He had previously comforted her with loving words, telling her not to fear separation. If he now breaks that promise and leaves, she argues that the fault does not lie with her for believing his reassuring words. The poem highlights that trusting a loved one's solemn promise is natural, and the blame for the broken trust rests entirely on the one who departs.

ai.literal: If [you would] prevent, prevent the separation of the beloved; otherwise, if he departs, reunion indeed [is] difficult.
ai.translation: If you would prevent anything, prevent the departure of my beloved; for if he leaves, a reunion will indeed be impossible.
ai.modern: தடுக்க நினைத்தால், அன்பானவரின் பிரிவைத் தடுத்து நிறுத்துங்கள்; இல்லையென்றால், அவர் பிரிந்து சென்றால் மீண்டும் இணைவது அரிது.
ai.explanation: In this verse, the heroine expresses the depth of her distress over her lover's impending departure. She urges her companion that if there is anything to be prevented, it must be his separation ('pirivu'). The word 'amaintār' refers to the lover who is perfectly suited and deeply intimate with her. She warns that if he departs ('nīṅkiṉ'), a future reunion ('puṇarvu') will be impossible ('aritu'), implying that she will not survive the grief of his absence.

ai.literal: If he is a hard-hearted person who speaks of separation, the hope that says 'he will bestow love' is impossible.
ai.translation: If he is so hard-hearted as to speak of parting from me, any hope that he will return to bestow his love is completely futile.
ai.modern: அவர் பிரிவைப் பற்றிப் பேசும் இரக்கமற்றவர் என்றால், அவர் மீண்டும் வந்து அன்பைச் சொரிவார் என்று நம்பும் நம்பிக்கை வீணானதாகும்.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the heroine expresses her despair to her companion upon hearing her lover talk of leaving. She describes him as 'van-kaṇṇar' (hard-hearted or cruel) because he is able to speak of separation without feeling her pain. She reasons that if he possesses such a cold heart, the hope ('nasai') that he will return to shower her with love ('nalguvar') is entirely futile ('aridu'). The verse highlights how the mere mention of parting shatters the heroine's trust in her lover's affection.

ai.literal: The lord of the shore's departure, will they not proclaim, the bangles that are slipping down from the wrist of my forearm?
ai.translation: Will not the bangles, slipping down from the wrists of my forearms, proclaim to the world that the lord of the shore has departed?
ai.modern: முன்கையின் மணிக்கட்டிலிருந்து கழன்று விழுகின்ற வளையல்கள், நெய்தல் நிலத் தலைவன் என்னை விட்டுப் பிரிந்து சென்றதை ஊராருக்கு வெளிப்படுத்திக் காட்டாவோ?
ai.explanation: The heroine is deeply distressed by the separation of her lover, the lord of the maritime tract (துறைவன்). Her intense grief and pining cause her body to waste away, making her arms grow thin. Consequently, the bangles on her wrists begin to slip off. She laments that even if she tries to hide her sorrow, these slipping bangles will loudly proclaim his departure to the entire neighborhood.

ai.literal: Painful is living in a town without companions; even more painful than that is separation from beloved ones.
ai.translation: Living in a town where one has no companions is painful; but far more painful than that is separation from those who are beloved.
ai.modern: உறவினர்கள் இல்லாத ஊரில் வாழ்வது துன்பமானது; அதைவிடத் துன்பமானது அன்பானவரைப் பிரிந்து வாழ்வது ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet compares two painful situations to highlight the extreme distress of separation. Living in a town without friends or relatives (இனன் இல் ஊர்) is hard and lonely. However, the poet states that separation from one's beloved (இனியார் பிரிவு) is even more painful (அதனினும் இன்னாது) than such a friendless existence. The words 'இன்னாது' (painful) and 'இனியார்' (sweet/beloved ones) beautifully contrast the bitterness of loneliness with the sweetness of love.

ai.literal: If touched, it burns, other than that, like the pain of love, if parted, can it burn, the fire?
ai.translation: Fire burns only when it is touched; but unlike that, can fire burn even when one departs from it, as the pain of love does?
ai.modern: நெருப்பு தொட்டால் மட்டுமே சுடும்; ஆனால் காமநோய் போல, விலகிச் சென்றால் சுடக்கூடிய வலிமை நெருப்புக்கு உண்டா?
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the heroine compares the pain of separation from her beloved to physical fire. She points out that fire only burns a person upon physical contact. However, the affliction of love (காமநோய்) behaves in the opposite manner, burning and causing intense suffering precisely when the lovers are parted (விடின்). By asking if fire can burn from a distance, she emphasizes that the torment of separation is far more powerful and painful than actual fire.

words.gloss: that which is difficult to bear

ai.literal: Enduring the difficult, removing the distressful disease, enduring the separation, staying behind and living afterwards, many are they.
ai.translation: There are many who can endure what is hard to bear, dispel the painful disease of grief, tolerate separation, and continue to live after their lover has departed.
ai.modern: தாங்குவதற்கு அரியதைத் தாங்கி, துன்பம் தரும் நோயை நீக்கி, பிரிவைப் பொறுத்துக் கொண்டு, காதலர் சென்ற பிறகு உயிர்வாழும் மனிதர்கள் பலர் இருக்கிறார்கள்.
ai.explanation: In this verse, the speaker highlights the extreme difficulty of surviving a lover's departure. She observes that there are many people who possess the strength to bear what is unbearable, overcome the painful sickness of longing, and continue living after separation. By pointing out that 'many' can survive this ordeal, she subtly reveals her own inability to do so, suggesting that for her, separation is a mortal blow.
